terms.grammar: construction: the verb in the second person singular, mostly subjunctive
evidence: Cic. Sen. 21: crēdō, nisi eam exerceās
Cic. Amic. 22: quīcum omnia audeās sīc loquī ut tēcum
terms.comment: The everyday way: “you”, meaning anyone, in the second person singular, in the subjunctive in a subordinate clause or a potential statement (nisi eam exerceās, if one doesn’t exercise it; crēderēs, you would have thought). Latin has no word for the pronoun “one”.

terms.grammar: construction: the passive, impersonally or with the thing as subject
terms.comment: ut dīcitur, as one says; ītur, one goes, people go; vīvitur, one lives.

terms.gloss: one, anyone (after sī, nisi, nē, num)
evidence: Petr. 34.1: sī quis nostrum iterum vellet mulsum sūmere

terms.grammar: construction: the verb in the first person plural
evidence: Catull. 22.21: sed nōn vidēmus manticae quod in tergō est
terms.comment: Where the speaker includes himself: nōn vidēmus, we (one) don’t see.

phrases.latin: at memoria minuitur. crēdō, nisi eam exerceās
phrases.english: But memory fades. — I suppose it does, if you don’t exercise it.

phrases.latin: quid dulcius quam habēre quīcum omnia audeās sīc loquī ut tēcum?
phrases.english: What is sweeter than to have someone to whom you dare say everything as you would to yourself?

phrases.latin: Māne quod tū occēperis negōtium agere, id tōtum prōcēdit diem.
phrases.english: Business you begin in the morning goes well the whole day.

phrases.latin: ad diaetam tuam ipsī mē, ut vērissimē dīcitur, pedēs dūcunt
phrases.english: My feet take me to your room by themselves, as is very truly said.

phrases.latin: suus cuique attribūtus est error; sed nōn vidēmus manticae quod in tergō est
phrases.english: Everyone has been given his own fault; but we don’t see the part of the bag that is on our back.

phrases.latin: sī quis nostrum iterum vellet mulsum sūmere
phrases.english: if any of us wanted another glass of honeyed wine
